Silver nanoparticles were synthesized by chemical reduction of silver nitrate using glucose as a reducing agent, yielding particles mostly between 1 and 100 nm in diameter.
Huntite/hydromagnesite minerals were used as non-halogenated flame retardants in the polymer composites.
Barium hexaferrite particles were synthesized by sol–gel method and used for radar absorbing properties.
Chitosan with molecular weight 150 kDa and 84.5% degree of deacetylation was used to impart self-healing properties.
Epoxy resin matrix was formed from epichlorohydrin and bisphenol-A cured with triethylenetetramine.
Composite coatings were applied on plastic, glass, and metal substrates for multifunctional testing.
Antibacterial activity was tested against Staphylococcus aureus (Gram-positive) and Escherichia coli (Gram-negative) using agar diffusion method.
Flame retardancy was evaluated by limiting oxygen index (LOI) and UL94 standard tests.
Radar absorption was measured by incorporating barium hexaferrite particles and testing microwave absorption.
Self-healing was investigated by incorporating chitosan and assessing crack repair capability.
FTIR spectroscopy confirmed the presence of organic components and interactions in composites.
SEM and XRD analyses characterized morphology and crystalline phases of the composites.
Silver nanoparticles showed shape- and dose-dependent antibacterial efficacy.
Huntite/hydromagnesite improved flame retardancy without halogenated compounds.
Barium hexaferrite particles exhibited low coercivity indicating particle size above superparamagnetic limit.
Chitosan-based self-healing involves UV-induced crosslinking of oxetane-substituted polymers.
Composite coatings showed synergistic effects, enhancing multiple functionalities simultaneously.
Surface profilometry quantified roughness of coated samples.
Adhesion strength of coatings was measured using scratch testing and converted to MPa.
The multifunctional composites were prepared by mixing additives at different loading levels into the epoxy matrix.
